summary: Master GIS and spatial analysis for agriculture. Learn to map crop health, assess food security, and forecast yields using QGIS and satellite imagery.
lede: Geospatial analytics for agribusiness combines satellite imagery, field data and spatial analysis to inform agricultural planning and food security assessments. For agricultural data analysts, food security officers and agronomists, the course covers monitoring crop health with vegetation indices, assessing land suitability using soil and terrain data, and mapping drought impacts and food vulnerability.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to integrate spatial data into agricultural planning and food security assessments.
modules: Foundations of Agricultural GIS and Spatial Data
Remote Sensing and Satellite Imagery for Agriculture
Vegetation Indices and Crop Health Monitoring
Terrain, Soil, and Land Suitability Modeling
Climate Variability and Drought Impact Mapping
Cloud-Based Spatial Analysis with Google Earth Engine
prerequisites: Participants must have a working knowledge of basic data management (e.g., Excel) and a fundamental understanding of agricultural or environmental concepts. Prior experience with GIS software is beneficial but not strictly required, as foundational tool navigation will be covered. A laptop capable of running QGIS (latest stable release) is required.
